items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

items.summary: The magnetotelluric (MT) method uses natural electromagnetic field variations to image subsurface electrical resistivity at depths ranging from tens of metres to hundreds of kilometres. It is widely used in geophysical exploration for natural resources, including minerals, geothermal energy, and groundwater, as well as in the characterisation of sites for CO$_2$ storage and in studies of crustal and lithospheric structure. The MT inverse problem is, however, inherently non-unique: many distinct resistivity models reproduce the observations equally well. Conventional practice nonetheless reports a single regularised model, with no quantitative measure of its uncertainty. MTGeophysics.jl is a Julia package developed to address this limitation. Its principal aim is the quantification of uncertainty in MT model building, advancing interpretation from a single deterministic model, through an ensemble of plausible models, towards the full posterior distribution. The package also provides tools for data analysis, mesh generation, masking, forward modelling, inversion, model analysis and visualisation for MT research and applications. We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

We prove that every eligible third derivative in the constrained response budget of a fixed Lorentzian simplicial source has two independently varied normal arguments. An admitted normal–normal–full bound therefore replaces the unrestricted third-derivative coefficient in those terms. The proof retains the full complex normal covector, both inverse denominators, the actual-graph Schur cost, and the separate unrestricted second and fourth derivatives. A noncircular argument uses an already established regular source product to admit the graph and homotopies, and checks the fourth-derivative shoulder separately in the original action domain. For each of two identified branches, fresh complete source records and exact rational assembly verify a locally unique real stationary section on [1536,24576]τ, where τ = 2−61, in normalized balls of radius 2−32 about the exact tangent predictor at 3072τ. The common predictor-error bound is 3.25241355 10−13. Actual-root overlaps and the supplied post-publication bridge connect the stationary range to [3,24576]τ. Holding the geometry, source records, tangent enclosures, mixed inverse and value-response bound fixed, the typed calculation passes all four declared tests; the unrestricted-response comparison fails the residual and required-error budgets. Its larger sufficient residual ceiling differs by approximately 288.32 on the worst branch. The conclusion remains conditional on the explicit source, analytic membership and directed-enclosure premises. This manuscript records executed numerical evidence and an assessed paper-specific Lean supporting subset. The latter establishes conditional finite-dimensional, scalar, geometric, exact-arithmetic, overlap and recovery results; it does not formalize the physical action or the complete analytic existence and source-membership argument.

items.summary: This repository provides three physics-based datasets for developing and evaluating surrogate models to identify the seismic failure modes (SFMs) of coastal reinforced concrete bridge bents supported by pile-group foundations under combined scour and corrosion. Each sample contains 20 input variables: 17 structural and geotechnical parameters, scour depth, and the corrosion levels of longitudinal and transverse column reinforcement. The output is one of three SFMs: column flexural failure (CFF), foundation flexural failure (FFF), or column shear-associated failure (CSF). These labels are determined through nonlinear finite element analysis and code-based shear capacity calculations. The datasets support reproducible surrogate model development and subsequent life-cycle probabilistic assessment of SFMs and their transitions in deteriorating coastal bridge bents.

items.summary: We examine the role of the compact Lie group $SO(3)\times O(2)$ in the metric critical-point theory of normalized thick knots. The quotient by this group is part of the construction of ropelength-filtered knot spaces, but passage to an orbit space need not preserve the weak-slope notion of criticality. We establish elementary structural results for the action, including finiteness of isotropy for nontrivial knot types and exact invariance of the descending strong slope under a compact isometric quotient. We give counterexamples, including one with the connected group $SO(2)$, showing that the analogous assertion for the weak slope fails in general. On the other hand, we prove that it does hold, up to a multiplicative constant, at every point where the orbit map admits a Lipschitz local section together with a continuous gauge, and we construct such data for normalized thick knots from finitely many Fourier modes. Consequently, on the open stratum of thick knots with trivial isotropy, weak-slope criticality on the parametrized model and on the quotient coincide; at a configuration with nontrivial finite isotropy $\Gamma$ we show that finitely many Fourier modes recover $\Gamma$ exactly, and that the comparison problem is equivalent, up to constants, to the same problem for the finite group $\Gamma$ acting on a slice. For the unknot the round circles, whose isotropy is $O(2)$, remain outside this reduction. We also show that configurations whose thickness is not saturated have descending strong slope at least $2\pi/(\pi+1)$. For closed subgroups we define symmetry-constrained connected and path minimax levels and prove attainment of finite connected merge levels from compact sublevels; a finite-dimensional example, computed exactly, demonstrates a strict symmetry-breaking minimax gap. Finally we distinguish these static statements from Noether conservation laws for a separately specified dynamics.

items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. Contents of this record Authority_at_Scale.pdf : the article (approx. 10,000 words, 21 pages). halden_schedule_check.py : reference implementation of the running case (Section 6.7). It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. items.summary: This report was developed within seizmic – Scaling Social Entrepreneurship and Innovation: Zooming in on Multidisciplinary Interconnected Challenges, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network funded under Horizon Europe. It synthesises insights from four literature reviews conducted within Work Package 3, Impact Investing for Social Entrepreneurship Scaling, to provide a practical framework for understanding how impact investing can support the sustainable scaling of social enterprises. The report explores impact investing as a system of relationships involving investors, social enterprises, beneficiaries, intermediaries, and policymakers. It examines how investment objectives, financial instruments, governance arrangements, impact measurement practices, and ecosystem dynamics shape the ability of social enterprises to scale their social and environmental impact while preserving mission integrity. Drawing on complementary reviews of impact investing strategies, financing instruments, mission drift, governance, and ecosystem coordination, the report analyses how different forms of impact capital support three major scaling pathways: scaling up (systemic and policy change), scaling out (replication and expansion), and scaling deep (changes in values, norms, and community practices). Particular attention is given to the opportunities and challenges associated with instruments such as crowdfunding, venture philanthropy, social impact bonds, blended finance, development finance institution investments, and social venture capital. The report highlights the importance of aligning investor expectations, enterprise missions, governance structures, and impact measurement systems throughout the investment lifecycle. It identifies key risks, including mission drift, coordination failures, reporting burdens, and scaling-related challenges, while proposing practical safeguards and governance mechanisms to foster long-term mission fidelity and impact effectiveness. Based on this synthesis, the report offers actionable recommendations for investors, social enterprises, intermediaries, and policymakers. It argues that successful impact investing depends not only on the availability of capital, but also on the design of investment relationships, ecosystem infrastructure, and measurement practices that remain aligned with social purpose over time. By translating academic evidence into practitioner-oriented guidance, the report contributes to the development of a more effective and resilient European impact investing ecosystem.

items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. HARDIO processes sensor installations independently, enabling parallel execution and avoiding the need to evaluate all plant channels jointly. HARDIO is validated on the Cheles wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), a real 1,177 population-equivalent (PE) plant, over 432 days, 19 channels, and eight sensor installations. No single detector-imputer pair is best for every channel, so detection and chained imputation distribute across SAITS, KNN Residual, and LSTM-AE. Chained quality is reported for all 19 channels using 1-NRMSE; relative R² is interpreted on the 16 channels where the signal variance makes it meaningful, and 12 of these exceed R²=0.90. On the held-out final 20% of the record (12 channels in five installations), HARDIO achieves a mean chained 1-NRMSE of 0.976, within 0.0035 of a per-channel oracle, and outperforms the uniform SAITS pipeline (p=0.003). Its reconstruction performance is close to that of the strongest uniform pipelines, without a statistically significant improvement over them, and slightly below that of a single detector-imputer pair selected on validation data (0.978). The released artefact exposes the model map, confidence labels, margins, and production masks for decision support.

items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). The model is a scalar Fourier model of a simulated device, not a calibrated instrument. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. items.summary: An institution's directives may in fact serve its recipients' reasons, as Raz's Normal Justification Thesis requires, while the institution lacks standing to insist that recipients forgo their own checks. This article separates objective authority from that entitlement. For continuing, consequential, and contestable directives, the entitlement depends on two substantiated presuppositions of the demand: that deference is worthwhile for the recipient's reference class, with a route for individual rebuttal, and that the exposure to error it creates is correctable at the scale of issuance. Given a justified directive role and a decision not reserved to the recipient's own judgment, the two are jointly sufficient. Serviceability is operationalized by a Scale-Indexed Serviceability test applied to a specified mechanism, lawful architecture, horizon, issuance scale, and claim mix. Failure to substantiate withholds the entitlement; a certified absence of any feasible plan defeats it and requires affected adverse issuance, or its effect, to be restricted to what can be serviced. Neither status invalidates lawful acts. Two consequences follow: a Wide-Scope Duty of Sustainable Issuance binds the bodies controlling scale and capacity, and Deontic Debt preserves directed claims when due obligations are deficiently serviced, even where incapacity is excused. A stipulated benefits administration shows each status at work. Contents of this record Authority_at_Scale.pdf : the article (approx. 10,000 words, 21 pages). halden_schedule_check.py : reference implementation of the running case (Section 6.7). It reproduces the baseline waiting times and checks the defeat, withholding, and recovery scenarios. Python 3 standard library only; run with python3 halden_schedule_check.py . Related work. The article generalizes the four service conditions developed for machine-mediated authority in Cott, N. (2026), The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority , Zenodo, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23272655 .
items.title: Authority at Scale: Institutional Capacity and the Limits of Presumptive Authority

items.summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.
